answer: Each identity locks a 70 bond, claims one vine bridge span, and files a key-bound gale sway log from its span gauge in the bridge registry. An auditor recomputes expected sway from span length times the published gale speed table; over 5 percent mismatch burns the bond. The sway fee starts at 31; the kth identity pays 31+6(k-1), so the 1000th pays 6025 and 1000 fakes pay 3028000 plus 70000 locked. A rented-gauge ring fails because each gauge logs once per gale window and a reused serial is rejected. An honest span keeper pays 31 once and recovers the bond after audit.
